sentences.literal: It governed seven counties, households three thousand eight hundred.〉
sentences.idiomatic: It administered seven counties and some three thousand eight hundred households.
A marquisate; the seat of its chancellor.

sentences.literal: 〈The place where Lu captured the unicorn.〉
sentences.idiomatic: Where Lu, it is said, took the kirin—the auspicious beast whose capture marked an age closing.

sentences.chinese: 方與 金鄉 湖陸[17]高平

sentences.literal: It governed three counties, households one thousand seven hundred.〉
sentences.idiomatic: It ruled three counties and about seventeen hundred households.
Once the heartland of the old state of Ren.

sentences.literal: It governed seven counties, households six thousand four hundred.〉
sentences.idiomatic: Seven counties fell under its authority, with roughly sixty-four hundred households.
A temple to Chiyou—the war deity of legend—stood there.

sentences.chinese: 范 無鹽 富城 東平陸 剛平
sentences.idiomatic: Fan, Wuyan, Fucheng, Dongpinglu, and Gangping.
The Jibei princedom—north of the Ji River

sentences.literal: It governed five counties, households three thousand five hundred.〉

sentences.idiomatic: Hometown of Bian Que, the healer of ancient renown.

sentences.literal: West of the county was Stone Gate.〉
sentences.idiomatic: West of the seat lay Stone Gate.

sentences.chinese: 臨邑 東阿 穀城

sentences.idiomatic: The hamlet called Wuxia lay within its bounds.

sentences.literal: It governed eleven counties, households nine thousand three hundred.〉
〈To the southwest was the Bright Hall.〉
sentences.idiomatic: The Bright Hall—the cosmic hall of state ritual—rose to the southwest.
Tortoise Mountain brooded on its lands.
It also held the Tuqiu cluster—the place the old histories name when a minister dreams of retiring.
Mount Chi reared up in the northeast.
Within it stood Zhuanyu—the small realm Confucius scolded a steward for failing to defend.
In older days, the polity of Mou.

sentences.chinese: 惠帝之末，兗州闔境淪沒石勒。
sentences.literal: At the end of Emperor Hui, Yan Province’s entire territory sank and was lost to Shi Le.
sentences.idiomatic: By the last years of Emperor Hui, not a handbreadth of Yan Province remained free: the whole region had fallen under Shi Le’s heel.

sentences.chinese: 後石季龍改陳留郡爲建昌郡，屬洛州。
sentences.literal: Later Shi Jilong changed Chenliu Commandery to Jianchang Commandery, belonging to Luo Province.
sentences.idiomatic: Afterward Shi Hu—Jilong by his intimate name—renamed Chenliu as Jianchang and folded it into Luo Province.

sentences.chinese: 是時遺黎南渡，元帝僑置兗州，寄居京口。
sentences.literal: At that time surviving people crossed south; Emperor Yuan established Yan Province in exile and lodged it at Jingkou.
sentences.idiomatic: Survivors poured south across the river; Emperor Yuan therefore “borrowed” a patch of land for a shadow Yan Province, its nominal seat at Jingkou.

sentences.chinese: 明帝以郗鑒爲刺史，寄居廣陵，置濮陽、濟陰、高平、太山等郡。
sentences.literal: Emperor Ming made Xi Jian regional inspector, lodged at Guangling, and set up Puyang, Jiyin, Gaoping, Taishan, and other commanderies.
sentences.idiomatic: Emperor Ming named Xi Jian inspector and moved the office to Guangling, carving out nominal jurisdictions—Puyang, Jiyin, Gaoping, Taishan, and more—on paper if not always on soil.

sentences.chinese: 後改爲南兗州，或還江南，或居盱眙，或居山陽。
sentences.literal: Later it was changed to Southern Yan Province, sometimes returning south of the Yangtze, sometimes dwelling at Xuyi, sometimes at Shanyang.
sentences.idiomatic: Renamed Southern Yan, it drifted: now back below the Yangtze, now perched at Xuyi, now at Shanyang—always provisional, like memory of a lost map.

sentences.chinese: 後始割地爲境，常居廣陵，南與京口對岸。
sentences.literal: Later they began to carve land as borders, usually residing at Guangling, south facing Jingkou across the shore.
sentences.idiomatic: Only later did real territory attach to the name; the inspectorate settled habitually at Guangling, its southern bank staring across the water at Jingkou.

sentences.chinese: 咸康四年，於北譙界立陳留郡。
sentences.literal: Xiankang fourth year, on the border of Northern Qiao they established Chenliu Commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xiankang they drew a Chenliu Commandery on the frontier of Northern Qiao—another line on the map where refugees might pretend the old heartland still existed.

sentences.chinese: 安帝分廣陵郡之建陵、臨江、如皋、寧海、蒲濤五縣置山陽郡，屬南兗州。
sentences.literal: Emperor Ai split from Guangling Commandery five counties—Jianling, Linjiang, Rugao, Ninghai, and Putao—and established Shanyang Commandery, belonging to Southern Yan Province.
sentences.idiomatic: Emperor Ai peeled off Jianling, Linjiang, Rugao, Ninghai, and Putao from Guangling to form a new Shanyang Commandery under Southern Yan—a fresh grid for an old grief.

sentences.literal: According to the Tribute of Yu it was the land between Jing and the River.
sentences.idiomatic: The Tribute of Yu draws it as the country between the Jing hills and the great river.

sentences.literal: The Rites of Zhou: “South of the river is called Yu Province.
sentences.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou declares: ‘South of the river lies Yu Province.’

sentences.chinese: 」豫者舒也，言稟中和之氣，性理安舒也。
sentences.literal: ” “Yu” means ease; it says they receive balanced harmonizing qi, nature and pattern calm and ease.
sentences.idiomatic: ‘Yu’ speaks of ease—of a region imbued with balanced breath, whose people grow temperate and unhurried.

sentences.chinese: 《春秋元命包》云：「鉤鈐星別爲豫州。
sentences.literal: The Spring and Autumn Yuan Ming Bao says: “The hook-and-hasp stars separately constitute Yu Province.
sentences.idiomatic: The apocryphon Spring and Autumn Yuan Ming Bao adds: ‘The hook-and-clasp stars mark out Yu Province among the fields of heaven.’

sentences.chinese: 」地界，西自華山，東至于淮，北自濟，南界荊山。
sentences.literal: ” The territorial bounds: west from Mount Hua, east reaching to the Huai, north from the Ji, south bounded by Mount Jing.
sentences.idiomatic: On earth its borders ran from Mount Hua in the west to the Huai in the east, from the Ji River northward to Mount Jing in the south.

sentences.chinese: 秦兼天下，以爲三川、河東、南陽、潁川、碭、泗水、薛七郡。
sentences.literal: Qin united the realm, making seven commanderies: Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Yingchuan, Dang, Sishui, and Xue.
sentences.idiomatic: When Qin swallowed the world, it sorted this ground into seven commanderies—Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Yingchuan, Dang, Sishui, and Xue.

sentences.chinese: 漢改三川爲河南郡，武帝置十三州，豫州舊名不改，以河南、河東二郡屬司隸，又以南陽屬荊州。
sentences.literal: Han changed Sanchuan to Henan Commandery; Emperor Wu established thirteen provinces; Yu Province’s old name was unchanged, but Henan and Hedong two commanderies belonged to the metropolitan inspectorate, and also they attached Nanyang to Jing Province.
sentences.idiomatic: Han rechristened Sanchuan as Henan; Emperor Wu’s thirteen circuits left the name Yu undisturbed even as Henan and Hedong passed to the capital intendancy and Nanyang was folded into Jing.

sentences.chinese: 先是，改泗水曰沛郡，改碭郡曰梁，改薛曰魯，分梁沛立汝南郡，分潁川立淮陽郡。
sentences.literal: Earlier, Sishui was changed to Pei Commandery, Dang Commandery was changed to Liang, Xue was changed to Lu; Liang and Pei were split to establish Runan Commandery, and Yingchuan was split to establish Huaiyang Commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: Already Sishui had become Pei, Dang had become Liang, Xue had turned into Lu; Runan was cut from Liang and Pei, Huaiyang from Yingchuan—the geometry of empire endlessly redrawn.

sentences.chinese: 後漢章帝改淮陽曰陳郡。
sentences.literal: Later Han’s Emperor Zhang changed Huaiyang to Chen Commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: Eastern Han’s Emperor Zhang traded the name Huaiyang for Chen.

sentences.chinese: 魏武分沛立譙郡，魏文分汝南立弋陽郡。
sentences.literal: Wei Wu split Pei to establish Qiao Commandery; Wei Wen split Runan to establish Yiyang Commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: Cao Cao—posthumously Wei Wu—split Pei to birth Qiao; his son Cao Pi, Wei Wen, split Runan to raise Yiyang.

sentences.chinese: 及武帝受命，又分潁川立襄城郡，分汝南立汝陰郡，合陳郡于梁國。
sentences.literal: And when Emperor Wu received the mandate, again he split Yingchuan to establish Xiangcheng Commandery, split Runan to establish Ruyin Commandery, and merged Chen Commandery into the Principality of Liang.
sentences.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the throne, he split Yingchuan again for Xiangcheng, Runan for Ruyin, and wove old Chen into the princedom of Liang.

sentences.chinese: 州統郡國十，縣八十五，戶十一萬六千七百九十六。
sentences.literal: The province oversaw ten commanderies and principalities, eighty-five counties, households one hundred sixteen thousand seven hundred ninety-six.
sentences.idiomatic: The province held ten commanderies and princedoms, eighty-five counties, and nearly one hundred seventeen thousand households on the books.

sentences.chinese: 統縣九，戶二萬八千三百。〉
sentences.literal: It governed nine counties, households twenty-eight thousand three hundred.〉
sentences.idiomatic: Nine counties, twenty-eight thousand three hundred households.

sentences.literal: 〈Han Emperor Xian made his capital at Xu.
sentences.idiomatic: Han’s last emperor once held court at Xu.

sentences.chinese: 魏禪，徙都洛陽，許宮室武庫存焉，改爲許昌。〉
sentences.literal: Wei abdicated the throne, moved the capital to Luoyang, Xu’s palace halls and armory remained there, and it was changed to Xuchang.〉
sentences.idiomatic: When Wei yielded to Jin and the capital flew to Luoyang, the old palaces and arsenals of Xu stayed behind—and the place was ennobled with the new name Xuchang.

sentences.chinese: 長社 潁陰 臨潁

sentences.idiomatic: Seats of the chancellor of a ducal fief.

sentences.chinese: 統縣十五，戶二萬一千五百。〉
sentences.literal: It governed fifteen counties, households twenty-one thousand five hundred.〉
sentences.idiomatic: Fifteen counties; twenty-one thousand five hundred households.
Created in the second year of Taishi.

sentences.literal: It governed seven counties, households eighteen thousand.〉

sentences.idiomatic: A marquisal seat with its chancellor.

sentences.literal: It had the western Bugeng wall.〉
sentences.idiomatic: It still guarded the western ramparts of Bugeng—the twin fortress the old Chu chronicles pair with its eastern sister.
On this ground Wei Wendi accepted the Han emperor’s yielding of the throne—the moment one dynasty’s flame passed to another.
